price_index_method: Motorsport price index = (CPI-U[y] / CPI-U[2025]) ^ 1.5, rounded to 3 decimals. CPI-U = BLS US city average all items annual averages (1982-84=100); 2025 = 322.1 (avg of H1 320.229 and H2 ~324.0), 2026 estimated at +2.8% (331.1). The exponent 1.5 means racing costs inflated ~1.5x as fast as general prices in log terms (~3.8%/yr vs ~2.5%/yr CPI over 1995-2025), calibrated so 1995 = ~0.33: a 1990s Late Model Stock program (~$50-60k) vs ~$150-200k today gives 0.28-0.40; tires, fuel, steel/aluminium, engines and transport rose faster than CPI (post-2001 fuel and post-2021 parts spikes). Top-level team budgets grew much faster still (Kulwicki's 1992 title on ~$2M vs ~$20M per Cup car in 2024, roughly 0.10) because of professionalisation, not price alone - apply an extra tier-specific 'arms race' factor for tier 6-7 budgets if desired (e.g. multiply by ~0.6 in 1995 rising linearly to 1.0 by 2015). Usage: nominal_cost(y) = cost_2025_dollars * price_index[y].
